overview: Help members better understand and manage their money through human-centered design and digital tooling, with a focus on increasing financial literacy and engagement.

sections.label: The Challenge
sections.headline: Members couldn't see the full picture of their finances.

cards.text: Bad UI eroded trust. Members switched banks when digital tools underdelivered.
One-size-fits-all apps overwhelmed users who wanted efficient, focused tools.
Lack of feedback loops meant products were built without real member insight.

features.label: Phase 01: Heuristic Evaluation
features.name: Heuristic Evaluation
features.headline: Finding the friction.
features.description: Used internal design guidelines to audit inconsistencies across account summary pages. Uncovered issues around clarity, hierarchy, and unauthenticated access.

features.label: Phase 02: Competitive Analysis
features.name: Competitive Analysis
features.headline: Learning from the best.
features.description: Compared USAA tools to banks and fintechs (Capital One, Simple, etc.) and built an internal research library to close gaps in competitor understanding.

features.label: Phase 03: Information Architecture
features.name: Information Architecture
features.headline: Structure that makes sense.
features.description: Ran IA tests using Treejack to restructure content based on real user behaviors. Simplified and consolidated account hierarchy across savings, checking, and credit products.

features.label: Phase 04: Prototyping & Testing
features.name: Prototyping & Testing
features.headline: Build, test, repeat.
features.description: Developed prototypes in InVision and tested with users via usertesting.com. Iterated based on feedback and performance analytics.

items.title: Design system alignment
items.description: saved dev time and increased modularity
